subject: English
description: Meanings of common and less-common phrasal verbs

questions.stem: Choose the meaning of the phrasal verb in: 'The manager decided to put off the meeting until next week.'
questions.explanation: 'Put off' = to postpone or delay something. Cancel = call off or drop entirely. Common confusable — 'put on' (wear clothes / gain weight / stage a show), 'put out' (extinguish a fire / publish a statement), 'put up with' (tolerate).
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the meaning of 'look down upon' in: 'She looks down upon people who don't share her opinions.'
questions.explanation: 'Look down upon' = to regard someone as inferior; to despise. Opposite — 'look up to' = to respect or admire. Related — 'look after' (take care of), 'look into' (investigate), 'look over' (inspect briefly), 'look forward to' (anticipate with pleasure).
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the meaning of 'bring about' in: 'The new policy has brought about a significant change.'
questions.explanation: 'Bring about' = to cause something to happen. Synonyms — cause, effect, produce, result in. Related — 'bring up' (raise a child OR introduce a topic), 'bring on' (cause something negative), 'bring in' (introduce / yield revenue), 'bring out' (reveal / publish).
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the meaning of 'cut down on' in: 'I need to cut down on my sugar intake.'
questions.explanation: 'Cut down on' = reduce the quantity of something. Stronger — 'cut out' = eliminate entirely (cut out sugar). Related — 'cut off' (stop abruptly / disconnect), 'cut in' (interrupt / join a queue ahead of others), 'cut back' (reduce — similar to cut down, used for services / spending).
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the meaning of 'break down' in: 'His car broke down on the highway.'
questions.explanation: 'Break down' (of a machine) = stop functioning. Other senses — (of a person) lose emotional control and cry; (of a substance) decompose chemically. Related — 'break up' (end a relationship / disperse a crowd), 'break out' (start suddenly — war, disease, fire), 'break in' (enter forcibly / interrupt / wear new shoes).
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the meaning of 'carry out' in: 'The scientists will carry out further tests before releasing the drug.'
questions.explanation: 'Carry out' = perform, execute, complete (a task, order, plan, experiment). Trap — 'carry' literally means 'to take', so students misread this as 'transport'. Related — 'carry on' (continue), 'carry off' (succeed in something difficult; also, take away as a prize or victim), 'carry over' (extend into a new period — leave days, balance).
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the meaning of 'fall out with' in: 'He fell out with his best friend over a trivial matter.'
questions.explanation: 'Fall out (with)' = have a serious disagreement that damages the relationship. Related fall- phrasals — 'fall through' (a plan failing), 'fall for' (be deceived by / fall in love with), 'fall back on' (rely on when other options fail), 'fall behind' (lag).
